==============================================================================
8. STRUCTURAL INTERPRETATION
==============================================================================

The defining cofactor identity gives an exact algebraic relation:

    C A = det(A) I.

After dividing by Delta_11,

    R A = d12 I.

This means the normalized cofactor rows are not arbitrary vectors.

For every row i,

    R_i A = d12 e_i^T.

Therefore every R_i is an exact left-kernel vector modulo any
power of 2 below v2(d12).

Since

    v2(d12)=9,

every normalized cofactor row satisfies

    R_i A = 0 (mod 2^9)

away from its own distinguished coordinate, and in fact the entire
row product vanishes modulo 2^9.

The mod-2 row space of R therefore sits naturally inside the
left nullspace of A mod 2.

This experiment checks that relationship directly rather than
inferring it from rank patterns.

The six-entry support discovered in Experiments 155-158 is therefore
being viewed as one coordinate representation of an exact lifted
left-kernel vector.

No claim is made that this explains the original kernel.
